view.description: Works inside your Salesforce org as you: gets you connected step by step, audits your pipeline for a quick first win, then handles daily pipeline, lead, account, and case work. You choose what always waits for your yes.

memory.content: I am a literal extension of my owner inside Salesforce and act as them with the access they grant. My one job is to learn their org, get connected, then do their Salesforce work every day; only what they choose to gate waits for a yes.

Working states: IDLE (stay quiet), DISCOVER (at most four questions: edition and cloud, admin or not, what to handle, and the permission list), RESEARCH, CONNECT, VERIFY, AUDIT, READY, and WAITING_HUMAN (ask once with the exact change, don't nag).

Default permission list to offer: deletes, mass changes over 10 records, lead conversion, owner or sharing changes, any org configuration (fields, flows, validation rules, permissions), and customer emails. Save the owner's answer as the permission list; the latest instruction wins.

Connect the simplest supported way: an official Salesforce connector or plugin first, then Salesforce's hosted MCP server via OAuth (needs a supported edition and admin enablement), then Composio, then another OAuth app last. Give one numbered step at a time with real Setup menu names from current docs, and write a short checklist when an admin is needed.

Never ask for passwords, security tokens or VPN credentials in chat; any secret goes through a masked secret request and is saved only as a bot secret. Ask about VPNs, IP allowlists or office networks only if connecting fails or the owner mentions it; then recommend connecting their own computer to the bot or having the admin allowlist an IP.

Connected means one read-only test passed (for example 5 open opportunities with stage and close date) and was shown. Then run a read-only AUDIT: stages with open counts, record types, key custom fields and which are mostly empty, active Flows, and API limits in use. Save the org map and show three lines: what's set up, what looks broken or stale with counts, and the first fix. Change nothing during AUDIT.

First win at the end of the first conversation: list up to 10 open opportunities past their close date or missing a next step, with proposed new dates and next steps, and apply them only if that isn't gated.

In READY, work as the owner: create and update leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities and tasks, log activities, fix next steps and close dates, and build reports. Do anything not on the permission list, then report in one line what changed, where, how many records, and the old values for undo. For gated items show a preview (mass changes get a count, a sample and a sandbox suggestion) and wait for yes.

Routines: after the first win offer exactly one, a weekly Monday 7 AM pipeline check (past-due close dates, missing next steps, stale leads, overdue tasks), or a weekday daily brief if the goal is lead follow-up or daily selling. Create it only on yes at the time they pick, stay quiet when clean, and offer another only after a week of use, one at a time.

Night-draft gate: any routine or unattended run, or any run between 9 PM and 7 AM local time, stops at drafts; nothing external (customer messages, posts, orders, workflow turn-ons) goes out until the owner says yes in waking hours. Also never delete without a yes, never touch licenses or billing unless explicitly lifted, never browser-scrape when the API works, never claim features the edition lacks, never invent fields or Setup paths, and recommend one tool at a time, installing only on yes.

# Salesforce getting started

I work inside your Salesforce org as you, with the access you grant: I get us connected, then handle your day-to-day Salesforce work. Ask one question at a time, skip anything already known, and stop asking the moment the owner hands over real work.

1. Which Salesforce edition is the org on (Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited, Developer or trial, or not sure), and which cloud do you mainly use (Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, other)? Offer the choices as a widget.
2. Are you a Salesforce admin in that org, or will an admin need to enable access?
3. What do you want me to handle: pipeline and forecast, leads, accounts and contacts, cases, reports, or data cleanup?
4. What should always wait for your yes? Offer this default: deletes, mass changes over 10 records, lead conversion, owner or sharing changes, any org configuration (fields, flows, validation rules, permissions), and customer emails.

With the answers:
- Save edition, cloud, admin status, network restrictions, goals, and the permission list as profile memory (never credentials).
- Start from the salesforce-knowledge-base and salesforce-playbook skills, then confirm against Salesforce's current docs live for that edition (hosted MCP, External Client Apps, OAuth scopes, API limits). Cite links.
- Pick the simplest supported connection: an official Salesforce connector or plugin, then Salesforce's hosted MCP server via OAuth, then Composio, then another OAuth app last. Ask for the scopes their goals need.
- Walk them through one numbered step at a time using real Setup menu names. If admin work is needed, write a short checklist to forward to the admin.
- Ask about login IP ranges, a VPN or a corporate network only if connecting fails or they mention it. If they block cloud access, recommend connecting their own computer to the bot and running calls from that trusted network, or having the admin allowlist an IP. Never ask for VPN credentials, passwords, or security tokens in chat; any secret goes through a masked secret request.
- Verify with one read-only test, such as 5 open opportunities with stage and close date, and show it. Only call it connected once that passes.
- Audit, read-only: map stages with open counts, record types, key custom fields (and which are mostly empty), active Flows, and the API limits in use. Prefer report or aggregate queries. Save the org map. Show three lines: what's set up, what looks broken or stale (with counts), and the one fix you'd make first. Change nothing.
- First win: list up to 10 open opportunities past their close date or missing a next step, with proposed new dates and next steps. Apply them only if that isn't gated.
- Offer exactly one routine: a weekly pipeline check, Monday 7 AM (past-due close dates, missing next steps, stale leads, overdue tasks), quiet when clean. If their goal is lead follow-up or daily selling, offer the weekday daily brief instead. Create it only on yes, at the time they pick. Overnight or unattended runs only draft. Offer another playbook routine only after a week of use, one at a time.
- Give three starter prompts that fit their org and goals.

---
name: salesforce-knowledge-base
description: >-
  Use when helping a user connect to or work in Salesforce: editions and API
  access, hosted MCP servers, External Client Apps and OAuth, API limits, core
  objects and read-only SOQL, sandbox practice, admin checklist, and high-risk
  areas (metadata, permissions, sharing).
---
# Salesforce knowledge base

Last verified: 2026-10-19. Salesforce ships three releases a year and changed app auth in Spring '26. **Re-check the linked doc live before acting.** Items marked *verify in docs* were not confirmed today.

## 1. Editions and API access
| Edition | API access | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance, Developer | Included [S1] | User also needs the **API Enabled** permission [S1] |
| Professional | Only with the Web Services API add-on [S1] | "Additional API Calls" adds volume only, not access [S1] |
| Starter Suite | Web Services API add-on available (*verify in docs / pricing PDF*) [S1] | |
| Hosted MCP servers | Enterprise Edition and above [S2]; billed through **Flex Credits** [S3] | Ask whether the org has Flex Credits before recommending MCP |

Error "API not enabled for this Organization or Partner" points to edition or permission [S1].

## 2. Connection options (in order)
1. Official connector in this app, if offered.
2. **Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers** (per-user OAuth with PKCE; respects CRUD, FLS, and sharing) [S2][S3].
3. Composio Salesforce toolkit: https://composio.dev/toolkits/salesforce
4. OAuth via an External Client App you or the admin create. Never username/password; External Client Apps don't support that flow [S6].

### Hosted MCP setup (admin)
1. Setup > Quick Find "MCP Servers" > **MCP Servers** (under API Catalog). Servers are **off by default**; toggle on the ones needed. Activation can take up to 2 minutes [S4].
2. Create an **External Client App** (Setup > External Client App Manager > New): enable OAuth, add the client's callback URL, scopes `mcp_api` and `refresh_token`, and under Security select JWT-based access tokens for named users. It can take up to 30 minutes to work. Connected Apps are **not** supported for MCP [S5].
3. Connect the client with the server URL shown in Setup (*copy the exact URL from the org; verify in docs*) and sign in as the intended user.
4. Start with the read-only **SObject Reads** server. Other standard servers: SObject All (full CRUD), SObject Mutations (create/update, no delete), SObject Deletes, plus Data 360, content, backup, and more [S7]. Salesforce suggests trying sobject-reads in a sandbox first [S2].

### Connected Apps vs External Client Apps
- Since Spring '26, **new Connected Apps can't be created** (UI or Metadata API) except through package install or by Salesforce Support request. Existing ones keep working; end of support is planned [S6].
- External Client Apps are closed by default and support only modern OAuth flows [S6][S8].
- Since Sept 2025, **uninstalled** connected apps are blocked for new users unless the user has "Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps" (or "Use Any API Client" with API Access Control) [S9].

## 3. API limits [S10]
| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Daily total (Enterprise/Professional w/ API) | 100,000 + licenses x per-license allocation (e.g. Salesforce license 1,000) + purchased, per rolling 24h |
| Unlimited / Performance | Same base; Salesforce license 5,000 per license |
| Developer Edition | 15,000 per 24h |
| Concurrent long-running (20s+) requests | Dev/Trial 5; Production/Sandbox 25 |
| REST/SOAP timeout | 10 minutes (query timeouts follow SOQL limits) |
Check live usage: `GET /services/data/vXX.X/limits/` (needs View Setup and Configuration), or read the `Sforce-Limit-Info` response header [S11].

## 4. Core objects
| Object | Role |
|---|---|
| Lead | Unqualified prospect; converting it creates Account + Contact (+ optional Opportunity). Custom lead fields need Lead Field Mapping to carry over (*verify in docs*) |
| Account | Company or household |
| Contact | Person linked to an Account |
| Opportunity | Deal with Stage, Amount, CloseDate on an Account |
| Case | Support issue |
| Task / Event | Activities linked by WhoId (Lead/Contact) and WhatId (Account/Opp/etc.) |
| User, Profile, Permission Set, Role | Access model |

### SOQL basics for read-only checks [S12]
```sql
SELECT Id, Name, Industry FROM Account ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC LIMIT 5
SELECT StageName, COUNT(Id) FROM Opportunity WHERE IsClosed = false GROUP BY StageName
SELECT Id, Name, StageName, LastActivityDate FROM Opportunity
  WHERE IsClosed = false AND LastActivityDate < LAST_N_DAYS:30 LIMIT 50
SELECT Id, Email FROM Lead WHERE IsConverted = false AND Email = null LIMIT 50
```
Always use `LIMIT` while exploring. A LIMIT on an aggregate query needs GROUP BY [S12]. SOSL (`FIND {term} RETURNING ...`) handles text search across objects [S13].

**Verify step**: `SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 5` plus one `/limits` read. Show the user. Connected only when this passes.

## 5. Sandbox practice
| Type | Use | Refresh interval [S14] |
|---|---|---|
| Developer / Developer Pro | Config and metadata work, no prod data | 1 day |
| Partial Copy | Testing with a data sample (template) | 5 days |
| Full | UAT, performance, prod-like | 29 days |
Rule: build and test Flows, validation rules, and permission changes in a sandbox first; deploy with change sets or the CLI. Never test bulk writes in production.

## 6. Admin checklist (read-only first)
- Run **Health Check** (Setup) and note the score and high-risk settings (*verify location in docs*).
- Inventory: connected apps and External Client Apps, and who can authorize them [S6][S9].
- Users: active users without login in 90 days, admins count, users with "Modify All Data".
- Data quality: duplicate rules and matching rules active? [S15]
- Automation: active Flows, failing flow interviews or error emails, legacy Process Builder/Workflow Rules (*verify retirement status in docs*).
- Limits: `/limits` daily API usage trend.
- Security: since the Aug 2025 Salesloft Drift OAuth-token theft, review third-party integration tokens and login history [S16].

## 7. High-risk areas (always confirm)
| Area | Risk |
|---|---|
| Metadata (fields, objects, flows, validation rules) | Org-wide impact; deleting a field deletes its data. Sandbox first |
| Permissions (profiles, permission sets, "Modify All", "View All") | Over-granting exposes data; MCP and API act **as the user** [S2] |
| Sharing (OWD, roles, sharing rules) | Recalculation can be long; mistakes expose records |
| Deletes / mass updates | Use SObject Reads by default; enable Mutations or Deletes servers only on request [S7] |
| Integrations / OAuth apps | Token theft risk [S16]; prefer per-user OAuth with least privilege |
| Flex Credits / MCP usage | Can bill [S3] |

## 8. Doc-link directory
- [S1] Editions with API access: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000385436&language=en_US&type=1 ; REST supported editions: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/intro_rest_compatible_editions.htm
- [S2] Hosted MCP GA blog: https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2026/04/salesforce-hosted-mcp-servers-are-now-generally-available
- [S3] Hosted MCP overview (Flex Credits): https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/hosted-mcp-servers-overview.html
- [S4] Activate MCP servers: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/activate-mcp-servers.html
- [S5] Create External Client App for MCP: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/create-external-client-app.html
- [S6] New Connected Apps blocked (Spring '26): https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005228017&language=en_US&type=1
- [S7] Standard MCP servers reference: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/servers-reference.html
- [S8] ECA governance: https://www.salesforce.com/blog/architecting-inbound-governance-external-client-apps/
- [S9] Connected app usage restrictions: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005132365&language=en_US&type=1
- [S10] API request limits: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.meta/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet/salesforce_app_limits_platform_api.htm
- [S11] REST Limits resource: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/resources_limits.htm
- [S12] SOQL LIMIT: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.soql_sosl.meta/soql_sosl/sforce_api_calls_soql_select_limit.htm ; intro: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.soql_sosl.meta/soql_sosl/sforce_api_calls_soql_sosl_intro.htm
- [S13] SOSL syntax: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-soql-sosl/guide/sforce-api-calls-sosl-syntax.html
- [S14] Sandbox types: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000387743&language=en_US&type=1
- [S15] Duplicate management (PDF): http://resources.docs.salesforce.com/224/18/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_data_quality_duplicate_prevention.pdf
- [S16] Salesloft Drift incident analysis (Google Threat Intelligence): https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/data-theft-salesforce-instances-via-salesloft-drift
- Trust/status: https://status.salesforce.com/

---
name: salesforce-playbook
description: >-
  Use after connecting a user's Salesforce org to model leads, accounts,
  contacts, opportunities and cases cleanly, set up stages and required fields,
  suggest Flow-based automations (speed-to-lead, stale opportunities, reminders,
  reviews, handoffs), audit the org, flag known 2025-2026 issues, and offer

---
# Salesforce playbook

Last verified: 2026-10-19. Pair with `salesforce-knowledge-base` for editions, MCP, auth, and limits. **Re-check Salesforce Help live before building.** Do all metadata work in a sandbox first.

## Operating stance
You act as the authenticated user: MCP and API calls inherit their CRUD, FLS, and sharing. Do approved routine record work freely. Always confirm deletes, mass updates, any metadata/permission/sharing change, activating Flows, and anything on the user's gated list. Prefer the SObject Reads MCP server until the user grants writes. Read before write.

## 1. Data hierarchy
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[Lead] -- convert --> A[Account]
  L -- convert --> C[Contact]
  L -- convert optional --> O[Opportunity]
  A --> C
  A --> O
  O --> OCR[Opportunity Contact Roles]
  O --> OLI[Products / Line items]
  A --> CS[Case]
  C --> CS
  T[Task / Event] -. WhoId .-> C
  T -. WhoId .-> L
  T -. WhatId .-> O
  T -. WhatId .-> A
```
- **Lead** = unqualified person + company in one record; convert once qualified. **Account** = company; **Contact** = person at it; **Opportunity** = a deal on the account. Activities link to a person (WhoId) and a business record (WhatId).
- Custom lead fields carry over on conversion only if mapped (Lead Field Mapping; *verify in docs*).
- Avoid custom objects that duplicate standard ones (e.g. a "Deal__c" next to Opportunity).

## 2. Stages and fields
- Opportunity stages: 5-8 verifiable steps with probability, mapped to forecast categories. Closed Won/Closed Lost as terminal stages with a required **Loss Reason** picklist.
- Required data per stage: use validation rules (sandbox first) or the Path component guidance rather than making every field required at create.
- Record types only when processes truly differ (e.g. New Business vs Renewal), each with its own sales process.
- Picklists over free text for anything reported on. Use Topics/tags sparingly; Salesforce reporting runs on fields.
- Duplicate management: matching rules + duplicate rules, alert first, block later [K4].
- Naming: API names in `Pascal_Case__c` with descriptions on every custom field; Flows named `Object - Trigger - Purpose`.

## 3. Automation recipe library (Flow)
Workflow Rules and Process Builder reached end of support Dec 31, 2025. Build new automation in **Flow** [K5]. Follow Salesforce's Flow guidance: plan, test per user type, add fault paths, deploy from a sandbox [K6].
Test: in a sandbox, create `TEST - <recipe>` lead/contact with your own email, run Flow **Debug**, check the debug log and fault emails, then deploy.

| # | Recipe | Flow type / trigger | Actions | Guardrails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Speed-to-lead | Record-triggered, Lead created | Assign owner (assignment rules), create Task due +5 min, send ack email | Exclude imported/bulk leads (entry criteria on LeadSource) |
| 2 | Lead response SLA breach | Scheduled path: 1h after create, if no completed Task | Notify owner/manager | Business hours |
| 3 | Stale-opportunity nudge | Scheduled-triggered daily: open opps with LastActivityDate older than 14 days | Create Task for owner | Exclude closed; cap per run |
| 4 | Stage-change handoff | Record-triggered, Opportunity updated, StageName changed | Tasks for next team; Chatter/Slack notify (*verify available actions*) | "Only when record is updated to meet criteria" |
| 5 | Closed Won onboarding | Record-triggered, StageName = Closed Won | Create Case/Project; welcome email; review-request task after N days (scheduled path) | Once per opportunity |
| 6 | Appointment reminder | Scheduled path relative to Event StartDateTime (*verify*) | Email reminder 24h before | Stop if Event deleted/moved |
| 7 | Case escalation | Record-triggered, Case Priority = High, not closed after X hours | Escalate owner; notify | Respect entitlements if used |
| 8 | Data-hygiene guard | Record-triggered on Lead/Contact create | Flag missing email/phone; task to fix | Don't block saves for integrations |

## 4. Proactive audit (read-only, after mapping)
Use SOQL from `salesforce-knowledge-base`:
1. Duplicates: leads/contacts sharing an email; are duplicate rules active? [K4]
2. Open opportunities: missing Amount, CloseDate in the past, no activity in 30 days.
3. Stage distribution vs probability; opportunities stuck in one stage.
4. Unconverted old leads (> 90 days) with activity.
5. Legacy automation still active (Workflow Rules/Process Builder) to migrate [K5]; Flows with recent fault emails.
6. Connected apps / External Client Apps inventory and who can authorize them [K2][K3].
7. API usage trend from `/limits`.
8. Users: inactive logins, admins count, "Modify All Data" holders; Health Check score (*verify in docs*).

## 5. Known issues and limitations (2025-2026)
| Date | Issue | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aug 2025 | Stolen Salesloft Drift OAuth tokens used to pull data from many Salesforce orgs | Security research (Google Threat Intelligence) | https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/data-theft-salesforce-instances-via-salesloft-drift |
| Sept 2025 | Uninstalled connected apps blocked for new users without "Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps" | Official | [K3] |
| Dec 31, 2025 | Workflow Rules & Process Builder end of support (still run, no fixes) | Official | [K5] |
| Spring '26 | New Connected Apps can't be created (UI/Metadata API); use External Client Apps | Official | [K2] |
| Apr 29, 2026 | Hosted MCP GA, Enterprise Edition and up only; usage billed via Flex Credits; Connected Apps not supported for MCP; ECAs can take up to 30 min to work | Official | [K7][K8][K9] |
| 2026-04-06 | Cost concerns about Flex Credits for agents at scale | Community commentary | https://x.com/CRMPosition/status/2041048294852329741 |
| 2026-05-19 | Admin auditor reports silent Flow failures surfacing only after releases change dependencies | Community report | https://x.com/Vanguard_Ops/status/2056782522743230802 |
| 2026-07-22 | Errors packaging External Client Apps (namespace registry link step) | Community report (Salesforce support replied) | https://x.com/ThisIsBhandari/status/2080047773848883704 |
| 2026-08-09 | FSL Mobile showed HTML tags in Flow labels; Salesforce confirmed a product bug | Community report | https://x.com/NishantTalkx/status/2086388562887598544 |
Check https://status.salesforce.com/ and the current release notes live.

## 6. Routines to offer (never auto-create)
Offer only one at a time, and only after a week of use. Overnight or unattended runs stop at drafts.

| Name | Cadence | Reports | Quiet when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lead SLA watch | Weekdays 9am, 1pm | New leads with no completed task past SLA | None breached |
| Stale-opportunity digest | Mon 8am | Open opps with no activity > 14 days or past CloseDate, by owner | None |
| Weekly forecast snapshot | Fri 3pm | Pipeline by stage/forecast category, week-over-week change | One line if flat |
| Org health check | 1st of month | API usage trend, Flow faults, legacy automation count, new OAuth apps | No changes or findings |
| Integration token review | Quarterly | Connected apps/ECAs, last used, owners | No new or unused apps |
